newsitem.title: CHINA: Hun Sen meets Cambodia King Sihanouk in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen meets Cambodia King Sihanouk in Beijing.

text.p: Cambodia's ruler Second Prime Minister Hun Sen met King Norodom Sihanouk in Beijing on Tuesday to seek the monarch's political blessing for his seizure of power last month.
A convoy of six cars carrying Cambodian flags swept Hun Sen and other senior officials past waiting reporters and into Sihanouk's tightly-guarded Beijing residence.
The prime minister arrived in the Chinese capital on Monday accompanied by newly-appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot, acting head of state Chea Sim and a delegation of government officials.

The meeting followed an offer to abdicate by Sihanouk, who has so far declined to endorse Hun Sen's rule, instead criticising Ung Huot as a "puppet" of Hun Sen and likening the current political situation in his country to a "comedy".

Analysts said Hun Sen, who seized sole power after ousting the king's son, co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in a bloody coup in July, would try to secure Sihanouk's political blessing to put the final stamp of legitimacy on his takeover.

Sihanouk had said he would meet Hun Sen and co-premier Ung Huot on Tuesday at his palatial residence, but only on a private basis. He has been in Beijing for medical treatment since February, but plans to return to Cambodia soon.

Sihanouk has hinted his strong disapproval of Hun Sen's actions and said on Monday he was ready to give up the throne as soon as he was confident that the second prime minister would not criticise him for doing so,.
Political analysts said the king's statement could be a signal he did not want any part of current events in Cambodia.
"I am ready to abdicate as soon as it will be possible for me to do so," the king wrote in a letter to his biographer and sent to news agencies.

In Bangkok, Ranariddh said he took his father's offer of abdication as an expression of disapproval of Hun Sen and slammed his opponent for pushing Cambodia into instability and toward the brink of another all-out civil war.
